Hey y'all!

json-as 2.1.0 is here! This release brings access-based lazy parsing, faster generated serializers, cleaner editor completions, and fixes across parser analysis, source bindings, and output ownership.

## Breaking changes

- **Lazy now means access specialization.** `@json` and `@json({ lazy })` decode the fields the program needs and scan past fields proven unused. Full reads and uncertain uses keep eager behavior, without deferred getters or typed-field source ranges.
- Removed `JSON.Lazy<T>`, instance-field `@lazy` / `@eager`, and the `"auto"`, `"all"`, `"none"`, and `"strategic"` class modes. Use plain field types and `{ lazy }` or `{ nolazy }` instead. AssemblyScript's built-in module/static `@lazy` is unchanged.
- `JSON_LAZY=false` replaces the old access-specialization and strategic-laziness flags. Whole-object serialization retains every field it emits and writes current values; typed fields no longer forward saved source slices. Dynamic `JSON.Value`, `JSON.Obj`, `JSON.Arr`, and `JSON.Raw` keep their existing source-backed behavior.

See the [2.1 upgrade guide](https://docs.jairus.dev/json-as/guide/upgrading-to-2-1) for migration details.

## What’s new

- Added compile-time field selection at eligible visible parse sites, with conservative eager handling for escaped objects, side effects, uncertain bindings, and analysis limits. ([#252](https://github.com/JairusSW/json-as/pull/252))
- Added `@json({ nolazy })` and `@json({ lazy: false })` as eager controls for a class and its descendants, including benchmark models.
- Hid internal runtime helpers from `JSON.` editor completions while preserving calls from generated AssemblyScript code, including optimized builds. The public entry points remain `JSON.parse`, `JSON.stringify`, and `JSON.validate`.

## Performance

- Improved numeric-row batching, integer formatting, string reservations, literal stores, Unicode scanning, and SIMD escape handling. Generated writers retain bounds, owning output, callback, and GC safeguards.
- Moved more decisions into the transform, including verified float-array metadata and generated serializer proofs. Unknown or redirected runtime bindings retain conservative paths.
- Updated the [benchmark charts](https://docs.jairus.dev/json-as/guide/performance). Classic deserialization now compares JavaScript, NAIVE, SWAR, SIMD, and simdjson owning structs. The published captures retain their original source and hardware metadata; retired deferred-field results are identified separately.

## Fixes

- Fixed access tracking through conditional assignments, loops, globals, helper defaults, argument evaluation, rest parameters, templates, `void`, and hoisted bindings.
- Preserved resolved type identity for generic targets and scalar aliases, including strict validation when an unread field has an incompatible JSON value.
- Bounded control-flow paths and helper expansion so difficult analysis falls back to eager parsing instead of consuming excessive compilation resources.
- Preserved application bindings and allocation hooks in generated writers, and retained snapshot Map iteration when callbacks can mutate the collection.
- Refreshed reviewed runtime fingerprints after formatting-only changes. CI now checks them before the transform suites, and packed-consumer failures report null diagnostics without masking the original error.
- Restored explicit compiler-warning exceptions instead of suppressing every warning with an empty list. AS201 remains enabled, with native, WASI, and test-build regression coverage.

## Testing

- The release workflow gates this GitHub release on all eight hosted test shards, including transform regressions, slow/fast parsing, strict parsing, npm/pnpm packed consumers, and package-content checks.
- Local validation includes the three-backend runtime suite, optimized lazy/API and helper-reachability checks, source/AST guards, and installed consumers across compiler runtimes.
- Lint and license-header checks remain enabled.

As always, try it, break it, and tell us what feels rough!
